title: Personal Checking: provisional credit when one dispute, or several, are submitted on the account
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Personal Checking account on which one or more electronic-transaction disputes are open. It fixes which accounts, and which dispute, fall under the single-dispute provisional credit rule, and what amount applies when several disputes are submitted at once.

## Formal clauses

1. **Exactly one submitted dispute.** The single-dispute provisional credit rule decides the provisional credit on an account that has exactly one electronic-transaction dispute in submitted status.
2. **The dispute under review.** The dispute under review is that single submitted dispute.
3. **Two or more at once.** When two or more disputes on the account are submitted at once, the provisional credit on each of them is decided under the general Personal Checking electronic dispute process alone, and the single-dispute rule posts nothing.
4. **Amount with two or more submitted.** On an account with two or more disputes in submitted status, the provisional credit amount of each dispute stays the dispute's claimed amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount.

## Count table

| Disputes on the account in submitted status | Dispute under the single-dispute rule | Provisional credit amount of each dispute |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one | That dispute | Decided under the single-dispute rule |
| Two or more | None; the single-dispute rule posts nothing | The claimed amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount; timing under the general electronic dispute process |
| None | None | — |

Only disputes in submitted status are counted. A dispute already provisionally credited, resolved or withdrawn does not count toward the total.

## Worked cases (hypothetical accounts)

- **One submitted, one already credited.** An account has one dispute in submitted status and one in provisionally credited status. Exactly one dispute is submitted, so that dispute is the one under review.
- **Two submitted.** An account has two disputes in submitted status: one claims 120.00 USD on a debit of 95.00 USD, the other claims 40.00 USD on a debit of 60.00 USD. Neither falls under the single-dispute rule. When each credit falls due under the general electronic dispute process, the first is 95.00 USD (the claim is higher than the disputed item's amount) and the second is 40.00 USD (the claimed amount).

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "with two submitted disputes, the single-dispute rule applies to the more recent one". **Correct basis:** with two or more submitted at once, the single-dispute rule posts nothing.
- **Wrong reading:** "with two submitted disputes, no amount rule applies". **Correct basis:** each dispute's amount stays its claimed amount, never more than the disputed item's amount.
